correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md:54–103: multiplication by a nonzero homogeneous quadric has rank one in each outer nonzero graded map by the complementary pairing, and middle map B has complementary coefficients. The square has rank 1 precisely when 2H is nonzero and the cube vanishes. If these ranks are R1,R2, the block counts are R2, R1-2R2 and 16-2R1+R2. For a nonzero rank-two hollow matrix, use the images of the four coordinate vectors in the nonsingular rank-two quotient form: they are zero or lie on one of its two isotropic lines, both of which must occur. This yields exactly the supported edges, stars and weighted K2,2 patterns; the latter has a rank-one cross block, three free nonzero entries and two equal nonzero matching products, so its hafnian is nonzero in odd characteristic. Rank one is impossible. In product coordinates X,Y,Z, the determinant is (X-Y-Z)^2-4YZ; the quadratic-character sum gives q^2 zeros, with 1 zero triple, 3(q-1) two-nonzero triples and (q-1)(q-2) all-nonzero triples. Each zero product has 2q-1 preimages, each other product q-1. The hyperplane H=0 cuts the cone into the binary equation X^2+XY+Y^2=0, giving exactly the stated number of rational lines using primitive cube roots or a double root in characteristic three. The independent H=0 count follows by a dot-product constraint. Subtracting yields all frequencies. Rank-three counts are positive by their factorizations. For rank four with H=0 take product triple (1,-1,0), with determinant 4; with H!=0 take (1,0,0), with determinant 1. These give positivity over every odd field, without relying on extension from a particular prime. The proof works for nonprime fields as stated. The phrase geometric branches is best read as rational branches over F_q; it is the number of rational lines that varies. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py: the listed prime-field exhaustive runs, weighted F_9 test and literal multiplication samples are finite corroboration only; the uploaded program was not executed.

value.rationale: This is the complete Jordan-type frequency classification for the natural first squarefree dimension in which a quadratic multiplier can have a nonzero square. It separates a natural invariant invisible to ordinary rank enumeration, and the dependence on cube roots of unity shows why a single polynomial in q cannot describe the joint law. The exact refinement is useful independently of any extension to more variables.
